clue.text: Extremely clever, but hateful

parts.note: damn is a slangy intensifier meaning very or extremely
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: Someone is grudgingly admired for brilliance while being loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely clever' reads as one compliment, but 'damn' is the slang intensifier, as in 'damn good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damnable deserves condemnation, so it is detestable.

clue.text: It takes about a minute, he believes, to clean the windscreen

indicators.note: the believer's word goes around, so it holds the minute's letter within it

parts.note: a deist is one who believes in God, described here by what he does
M is the standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A believer pauses briefly before wiping the car's windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: Demisting is clearing condensation from glass, as on a car's front window.

clue.text: Instruction book for organ keyboard

definitions.meaning: an organ's keyboard played by the hands, as opposed to the pedals

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a handbook and a hand-played keyboard on an organ.

clue.text: Tea cartel involved in dispute

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled together, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tea-trading cartel is caught up in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to quarrel or argue heatedly, a verb like dispute.

clue.text: Tennyson's joint office

parts.note: Tennyson held the post of national poet; 'joint' hints at a vessel, as if the job were a boat Tennyson shared

explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson was Poet Laureate, so his official post was the poet's crown office.

clue.text: "Respectable Professors of the ____ Science" (Carlyle)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Carlyle mocked economists as professors of a gloomy science

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank before 'Science'; the missing word completes Carlyle's famous phrase for economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlyle nicknamed economics the gloomy science, his adjective meaning bleak or depressing.

clue.text: Batting place needs filling

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
to lay is to put or place

explanation.surface: A cricket batting position needs someone to fill it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is IN. An inlay is also a dental filling.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlay is material set into a cavity, as in a tooth filling.

clue.text: One in a temper gets hurt first in a match

indicators.note: the hurt's word is placed at the front, before the rest

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: the single figure is placed within the word for temper

parts.note: rage is a fit of temper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone losing their temper is injured early in a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a temper' reads as an angry person; 'in' signals the insertion, and 'first' sends the hurt to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a union of two people, which is a wedding or wedlock.

clue.text: Song by a dweller near the springs of Dove is heard with clarity

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken out loud and gives the sound of the entry

parts.words: Song by a dweller near the springs of Dove
parts.note: Wordsworth's Lucy 'dwelt among the untrodden ways beside the springs of Dove', so a song about her is a Lucy ditty

explanation.surface: A Wordsworthian rustic's song rings out clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's Lucy poems describe a girl who lived by the River Dove; LUCY DITTY spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clearness of expression or thought.

clue.text: Bull-headed chap, a youngster without character in Crete

indicators.note: in old usage without means outside, so the youngster's word encloses the letter

parts.note: a minor is someone under age
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Crete

explanation.surface: A stubborn man and a boy with no personality are found on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking. The Minotaur lived in the Cretan labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth was a man with a bull's head.

clue.text: Minister in the Magic Circle

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman belongs to the conjurors' society, the Magic Circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a famous British society of magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a clergyman, which a minister of religion is.

clue.text: One getting up from a well sprung mattress

definitions.text: One getting up from a well sprung mattress

parts.words: One getting up from a well sprung mattress
parts.note: reads as someone rising from bed, but means a performer bouncing upwards on a springy mat

explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who bounces on a sprung canvas frame performs leaping routines.

clue.text: The way to ventilate this sort of case

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to air a room is to ventilate it

explanation.surface: Advice on how to freshen up some sort of container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this sort of case' refers back: the answer plus 'case' makes a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is the set of steps a stair word plus case names.

clue.text: One arriving in good time for breakfast

definitions.text: One arriving in good time for breakfast

parts.words: One arriving in good time for breakfast
parts.note: read as a punctual guest at the table, but recalls the proverb about catching the worm

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises or arrives early is said to be like the bird that catches the worm.

clue.text: Foul-mouthed women's crew, lighter than a feather

parts.note: foul spoken sounds like fowl, and a bantam is a small fowl
W is the abbreviation for women
a rowing crew is an eight

explanation.surface: A rowing team of sweary women boasts about being slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul-mouthed' means 'fowl' said aloud, and a bantam is a small chicken. In boxing, bantamweight is the division below featherweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantamweight is the boxing class immediately below featherweight.

clue.text: Wizard bagpipe player bears an English name

indicators.note: in a down entry, what bears something has it sitting above, so the abbreviations come on top

parts.note: the chanter is the pipe of a bagpipe on which the melody is played

explanation.surface: A magical piper carries an English name.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter is a sorcerer who casts spells.

clue.text: Bad habit one puts up with inside is intolerable

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the rearranged letters
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled
in a down entry, putting up means writing the word upwards

parts.note: cum is Latin for with

explanation.surface: A bad habit that someone puts up with becomes unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' makes ABITH, and 'puts up' turns the Latin word upwards in this down entry; 'inside' places it before the final letter. 'one' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a bit much is excessive, more than one can bear.

clue.text: Cabaret artiste becoming thinner

definitions.meaning: a performer who undresses on stage

explanation.surface: A nightclub performer shedding weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an undressing performer and a paint-removing solvent.

clue.text: Ram alcohol into the sweet

parts.note: a ram is something that butts, a butter
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Instructions to force liquor into a confection.
explanation.walkthrough: A ram butts, so it is a butter (one who butts).
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee confection.

clue.text: Vehicle needing a lot of bodywork?

definitions.text: Vehicle needing a lot of bodywork?

parts.words: Vehicle needing a lot of bodywork?
parts.note: bodywork reads as panel repairs, but this vehicle's work is carrying the dead

explanation.definitionFit: A funeral car carries coffins, so its job involves bodies.

clue.text: Bait badger

explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to torment and to pester, both senses of the two clue words.

clue.text: Harris. George and I guiding the ship of state?

definitions.text: Harris. George and I guiding the ship of state?

parts.words: Harris. George and I guiding the ship of state?
parts.note: Harris, George and the narrator are Jerome's Three Men in a Boat; three men steering the state is a ruling trio

explanation.surface: Jerome's boating trio take charge of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris, George and J are the Three Men in a Boat; in ancient Rome three men jointly ruling formed a ruling body of three.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumviri were three magistrates sharing power in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Use timer switch to cut corners

indicators.note: to switch things round is to change their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to use a timer to save effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut corners' suggests skimping, but it means joining at an angle, as with a picture frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitre is to cut angled ends so two pieces meet at a corner.

clue.text: Tree indicates start of Christmas in the neighbourhood

indicators.note: the initial letter is placed within the word for neighbourhood

parts.note: an area is a district or neighbourhood

indicators.note: only the first letter of Christmas is used

explanation.surface: A tree heralds the coming of Christmas locally.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a palm tree, source of the betel nut.

clue.text: Ruth, starting at university, becomes snobbish

indicators.note: the university word comes at the start, ahead of the rest

parts.note: being up means in residence at university
ruth is an old word for pity

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth goes to university and becomes stuck-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a name, but it is the old noun for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means self-important or arrogant.

clue.text: Climber knew a round song

parts.note: wist is the archaic past tense of wit, to know
an aria is a song, a full rounded solo

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a round they once sang.
explanation.walkthrough: WIST is an old word for knew.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria is a climbing plant with hanging flowers.

clue.text: Insect nesting in mesh or net curtains

indicators.note: something nesting in is lodged inside, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A wasp has made its nest in the mesh of some net curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large wasp.

clue.text: Flora Poste's cousins, abandoning tot, are exposed

indicators.note: the cousins give up the letters for tot, which are removed from their name

parts.note: the Starkadders are Flora Poste's relatives in Cold Comfort Farm
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Flora Poste's relatives leave a toddler behind and are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but is the verb 'add'. Flora Poste is the heroine of the novel Cold Comfort Farm. STARKERS is British slang for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for completely naked.
